newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: S&P puts Lloyds NZA on creditwatch positive.
newsitem.headline: S&P puts Lloyds NZA on creditwatch positive.

text.p: Standard and Poor's on Tuesday said it had put Lloyds Bank NZA Ltd's AA- long term rating on creditwatch positive following the announcement of Lloyds NZA's impending acquisition by ABN Amro Australia.
S&P also affirmed Lloyds NZA's A-1+ short term rating, as well as ABN Amro Australia's long term AA and short term A-1+ ratings.
S&P said ABN Amro Australia's ratings were based on the blanket guarantee provided by its parent, ABN Amro Bank N.V. (of the Netherlands) and the parent bank's strong financial standing.

"The ABN Amro group benefits to a large degree from its dominant position as the premier lender and investment banker to the major corporations in the Netherlands and has been able to maintain satisfactory levels of operating profitability and capital," S&P said.

"ABN Amro's capital ratios are in line with those of other major international banks, particularly if the bank's hidden internal reserves are included. It is expected that the Dutch banks will make these reserves public at year-end 1996."
